rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 (outer sensors at x = ±0.06, sensor_size 0.016, kp 7.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.0) is the best raced design at 64.74. Iteration 7 changed only kp, to 6.5, and scored 53.37. Its s-bend progress fell back from 0.140 to 0.059, with s-bend score spread from 18.1 to 59.2, so kp is contributing to the bend stall. Oval steering_oscillation was unchanged at 0.1589, so the kp drop did not reduce oscillation. The Evaluator's branch (b) applies: return to kp 7.0 and reduce oscillation through kd instead.

Change. kp goes back to 7.0 and kd rises from 0.2 to 0.3, the Evaluator's suggested kd range. Relative to the best design (iteration 6), this is a single-group change to kd. Geometry (outer sensors at ±0.06, sensor_size 0.016), base_speed 1.4, ki 0.0, the weights and line_loss last_direction are unchanged.

Expected result. s-bend progress returns near 0.14, and steering_oscillation falls below about 0.16 on the oval and s-bend because the derivative term damps the response. Max_error should stay near 0.06 m.

Hypotheses. (1) If oscillation falls and s-bend progress holds at about 0.14, kd is the right lever. The next single-group test is line_loss search_right, since slalom has lost the line once per run in every race with progress stuck near 0.10. (2) If kd 0.3 adds jitter without lowering oscillation, the derivative is amplifying sensor noise, so return to kd 0.2 and accept the oscillation. (3) If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a later single-group revision.

Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track (oval, s-bend, slalom), plus completion_time and rms_error. These separate the oval trade-off from the slalom line loss.
